title: A practical efficient approach in high throughput screening: using FDR and fold change
protocol: Collect raw luminescence measurements from each well of the high throughput screen and record as numeric values.
Record well location and plate number for each measurement.
Normalize numeric luminescence values to internal reference control samples on each plate.
Divide the value of each experimental well by the corresponding reference well value.
Perform a two sample t-test with pooled variance for each gene to determine the significance of differences between mean values under two experimental conditions.
Record the P-value obtained from the t-test.
Use GeneSpring and SAS software to perform the test, as results are nearly identical with minor decimal rounding differences.
Consider using alternative statistics such as S- (SAM), U- (Mann–Whitney), or M-statistics for calculating P-values.
For multiple experimental conditions, use ANOVA-type analysis to calculate P-values.
With the generated P-values, perform Benjamini-Hochberg's method to control the false discovery rate (FDR).
Use GeneSpring and SAS standard operations for FDR control.
Inflate raw P-values based on their rank in the distribution of all P-values.
Calculate the FDR for each gene using the formula FDR\(_i_)= P\(_i_) \(_m/i_), where \(P\(i)_\) is the P-value of gene _i_, and _i_ is its rank, with _m_ as total number of comparisons.
Select genes into list A if their FDR is less than or equal to 0.05.
Sort viability ratios in ascending order.
Select genes with a fold change among the lowest 2.5 percentile into list B.
Include genes identified by both list A and list B in list C.
Validate and functionally test genes in list C using either FDR or fold change.
